newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares rise to new record on high volume.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares rise to new record on high volume.

text.p: Russian shares notched up another record on Friday but came off morning highs to end the day with only modest gains over Thursday, dealers said.

The Russian Trading System (RTS) 24-share index ended at 291.98, up 1.21 percent on Thursday's closing 288.49, on strong volumes for all-share trading of $60.15 million, the national brokers association NAUFOR said.
However, the index ended off its intrasession high of 293.33, recorded at 1300 GMT, and some dealers said the strong volumes -- the second highest on record -- showed profit-taking was setting in.
"Everyone recalls that the market can't constantly move vertically," said Andrei Kukk, head of equities at Rinaco Plus.
"Everyone was taking some sort of profit, but in different stocks at different times."
But Kukk noted that strong buying meant the correction barely affected some shares, with the bid quote for Norilsk Nickel rising to $6.86 from $6.75 at Thursday's close.
Nevertheless, the febrile buying seen at the start of the week, has subsided, while every buyer found a seller, dealers said.
"People realised they were more frightened of losing money than not satisfying clients," Kukk said.

One of the most volatile stocks on Friday was Irkutskenergo, which finally launched its ADR. The utility closed at $0.285, with quotes of $0.265/0.285, after soaring in early trade over $0.300 from Thursday's closing $0.242.
Shares of Russian companies which have issued ADRs have generally outperformed the market, and Irkutskenergo has advanced strongly in recent weeks in anticipation of the ADR.
Rumours of the ADR launch started to circulate on Thursday night, allowing some operators to buy early and sell into the rising market, but leaving others with hefty losses.
But not all traders believe the bull run is over.
United City Bank senior trader Samit Yakovlev said the correction was largely due to end-week position squaring and the market would resume its advance on Monday.
"I think many people grasped this correction today as an opportunity to buy," he said.
